transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling card customer support. How can I help you today?
Customer: Hi, I'm calling because I was looking over my recent activity and there's a charge from Paperloom Studio that doesn't look right.
Agent: I can certainly look into that for you. May I have your name, please?
Customer: Yes, my name is Mei Lindqvist.
Agent: Thank you, Ms. Lindqvist. For security purposes, could you confirm the billing zip code on your account?
Customer: Sure, it's 98103.
Agent: Thank you. I have your account pulled up. Could you tell me the date and the total of the transaction you're questioning?
Customer: The charge was on September 19th, and it was for $267.00.
Agent: Got it, September 19th for $267.00 from Paperloom Studio. Did you receive a statement with this charge?
Customer: Yes, it showed up on my statement from September 29th, which was sixteen days ago.
Agent: All right. Can you walk me through what happened with this purchase?
Customer: Well, I bought an art print on their website. It was eighty-nine dollars. The package arrived fine and had the one print inside, but when I saw the $267.00 total on the card, I realized they charged me for three of them instead of one.
Agent: Did you place three separate orders, or was it a single order online?
Customer: It was just a single order. I only ever selected one print in my shopping cart.
Agent: Have you reached out to Paperloom Studio about this charge yet?
Customer: I sent an email to their customer service address last week with a picture of the packing slip, but I haven't heard anything back from them.
Agent: What did the packing slip say regarding the quantity of items?
Customer: The slip in the box listed quantity one for the print, and only one print was actually in the box.
Agent: So just to make sure I have all the facts noted down correctly: on September 19th, you purchased a single print from Paperloom Studio, received that one item, but the charge that appeared on your September 29th statement was $267.00, which reflects a charge for three prints.
Customer: Yes, that is exactly what happened.
